## Design

### 2026-10-01 — Today, I worked on my Smart Workshop Sensor project. The goal of the project is to build a small and useful device that can measure and display different environmental values in a workshop, garage, or

**5h**

Today, I worked on my Smart Workshop Sensor project. The goal of the project is to build a small and useful device that can measure and display different environmental values in a workshop, garage, or room.

First, I planned the main features of the project and decided which components I would need. The main components are an ESP32 microcontroller, a BME280 sensor, an OLED display, and a BH1750 light sensor. I also planned to use buttons and LEDs to create a simple user interface and status system.

After planning the hardware, I created a complete parts list and checked the estimated costs. One important requirement is that the complete project should cost no more than 65 US dollars. I therefore focused on affordable components while still trying to keep the project reliable and useful.

I also planned the software structure for the ESP32. I want to program it using C++ with PlatformIO in Visual Studio Code. The device should show temperature, humidity, air pressure, and light intensity on the OLED display.

Finally, I started planning the 3D-printed enclosure. It should be compact, clean, and practical, with openings for the sensors and space for the display, buttons, and LEDs.

Overall, today I focused mainly on planning, researching components, and designing the basic concept of the project.
